clue.text: Final part of record produced just in time

parts.note: the final one in a series is the last
a minute is one entry in the minutes, the written record of a meeting

explanation.surface: The closing section of a recording was finished only just before the deadline.
explanation.definitionFit: Something last-minute is done or made at the latest possible moment, barely in time.

clue.text: Need a lot of Indians, say

indicators.note: say tells us the word is to be spoken, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: a lakh is a hundred thousand in Indian usage, so a lot of Indians could be a lakh of them

explanation.surface: A request for a large number of people from India.
explanation.walkthrough: LAKH, the Indian word for a hundred thousand, is pronounced like LACK.
explanation.definitionFit: To need something is to be without it, the same as a want or shortage.

clue.text: No men lost at sea falling asleep

indicators.note: at sea means confused or all over the place, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Sailors drowned in a shipwreck while dozing off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' rearranges NO MEN LOST.
explanation.definitionFit: Somnolent means drowsy, on the point of dropping off to sleep.

clue.text: Nautical work bringing captain and sailor money

parts.note: the master is the captain of a merchant ship
a man is an ordinary member of a ship's crew
ready (or the readies) is slang for cash

explanation.surface: A seafaring job paying a ship's captain and a crew member.
explanation.walkthrough: Masterman Ready is an 1841 sea story for children by Captain Frederick Marryat.
explanation.definitionFit: This Marryat novel is about a shipwrecked family and an old seaman, so it is a nautical book.

clue.text: Love is not good without husband at home?

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the first words go round the others

parts.note: taken as written
H is short for husband, as in genealogy tables
someone at home is in

explanation.surface: Is a man who stays home with his wife not a decent fellow?
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside. In tennis, love means a score of zero, which is the trick of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Love is the tennis score of zero, so it means none at all.

clue.text: Driver taking Aussie's fare without right

indicators.note: without as in outside: the food word goes around the letter for right

parts.note: tucker is Australian slang for food

explanation.surface: A motorist picks up an Australian passenger without permission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fare' looks like a taxi passenger; it is food, TUCKER, which goes around R.
explanation.definitionFit: A trucker drives a lorry for a living, so is a professional driver.

clue.text: Learner in academic stream still

indicators.note: in places the learner's letter inside the river

parts.note: the Cam is the river running through the university city of Cambridge
L is for learner, as on the L-plates of British learner drivers

explanation.surface: A trainee student is placed in a set at university without moving on.
explanation.definitionFit: Still water is calm, undisturbed and without movement.

clue.text: Steer clear of a heartless situation, say

parts.note: in bridge a void is holding no cards of a suit, so having no hearts is one example

explanation.surface: Keep away from a sad, unfeeling predicament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' looks like unkind, but it is the bridge sense: a player with no hearts has a void in that suit.
explanation.definitionFit: To avoid something is to keep away from it or evade it.

clue.text: Playing down note I perform musically

parts.note: a minim is a musical note, a half note
to sing is to perform music with the voice

explanation.surface: A musician downplays a single note before singing it.
explanation.definitionFit: Minimising a matter means making it seem smaller or less important than it is.

clue.text: Representative characters found in (St.) James

parts.note: foreign envoys are accredited to the Court of St James's, and Henry James wrote a novel named after such figures

explanation.surface: Typical figures who appear in the writing of a man named James.
explanation.walkthrough: Two readings: diplomats posted to the British court (the Court of St James's), and Henry James's 1903 novel.
explanation.definitionFit: The title of a Henry James novel, whose name is also what envoys at the Court of St James's are called.

clue.text: Penniless university position for author

indicators.note: without a penny, so the letter P, short for penny, is removed

parts.note: a campus is the grounds and location of a university

explanation.surface: A broke academic wants a post as a writer.
explanation.walkthrough: Albert Camus was the French author of The Outsider.
explanation.definitionFit: Albert Camus was a French novelist and Nobel laureate, an author.

clue.text: Try for this at end of flight

definitions.meaning: in rugby a try is scored by grounding the ball over the line, and in American football a try follows such a score

explanation.surface: Aim for this when a plane journey finishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for this at' simply joins the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: A rugby try is a grounding of the ball, and an aircraft's landing is the same word.

clue.text: Adventurer took horse some hay by chance

parts.note: to take horse is to ride, and in the past tense one rode
a rick is a stack of hay
at random means by chance

explanation.surface: An explorer rode off with a stack of hay at random.
explanation.walkthrough: The Adventures of Roderick Random is Tobias Smollett's 1748 novel.
explanation.definitionFit: The hero of Smollett's novel is a roving adventurer, so the name stands for one.

clue.text: Stopped getting involved in debt and courts

indicators.note: involved means tangled together, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Halted because tangled up in money owed and legal proceedings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting involved' scrambles DEBT and COURTS together.
explanation.definitionFit: To be obstructed is to be blocked, held up, stopped.

clue.text: Drink container British always cram?

parts.note: e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, meaning always
to mug up is to cram for an exam

explanation.surface: A British student is forever swotting for exams over a pint.
explanation.walkthrough: MUG (up) is British slang for studying hard.
explanation.definitionFit: A large handled vessel used for drinking ale is a drink container.

clue.text: They remove lead from sections of bridge

definitions.meaning: erasers wipe out pencil marks, the lead of a pencil

explanation.surface: Workers strip lead off parts of a bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: In British English an eraser is called a rubber.
explanation.definitionFit: Erasers rub out graphite, and a rubber is a set of games in bridge.

clue.text: Converted on email to showing passion

indicators.note: converted means changed into another form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Persuaded by a heartfelt message sent online.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Converted' rearranges ON EMAIL TO.
explanation.definitionFit: An emotional person displays strong feelings openly.

clue.text: Like red wine — half-heartedly bottling it in old vessel

indicators.note: bottling means holding something inside, so the other word goes inside
the heart of the word is its doubled middle letter, and half of that is removed

parts.note: red wine is tannic, rich in tannin
taken as written

explanation.surface: A red wine, only half-enjoyed, is bottled on an ancient ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-heartedly' drops one of the two middle Ns, leaving TANIC; 'bottling' then holds the other word inside it. Tannin gives red wine its dry taste.
explanation.definitionFit: The Titanic was the liner that sank in 1912, an old ship.

clue.text: Something to eat that's excellent and cold inside

indicators.note: inside tells us the letter for cold goes within the other word

parts.note: choice means of excellent quality
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A treat that is first-rate with a chilly centre.
explanation.walkthrough: A choc-ice is a British ice-cream bar coated in chocolate.
explanation.definitionFit: A choc-ice is a chocolate-covered ice-cream bar, a snack.

clue.text: Degrees shown by early instrument

parts.note: BAs are Bachelor of Arts degrees
soon means before long, early

explanation.surface: Academic qualifications gained by a primitive device.
explanation.definitionFit: The bassoon is a low-pitched woodwind instrument.

clue.text: Bishop with English church accepting his responsibility to pray

parts.note: B is short for bishop in chess notation
a see is the diocese a bishop is responsible for

explanation.surface: A bishop with the English church takes up his duty to pray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'his' refers back to the bishop, whose area of charge is called a see.
explanation.definitionFit: To beseech is to beg earnestly, to pray in the old sense of request.

clue.text: Book accommodation for servile type

parts.note: an Uncle Tom is a slur for someone too submissive to those in power; with the possessive this gives the 's
a cabin is a simple dwelling or a room on a ship

explanation.surface: Reserve a room for a subservient person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' links the dwelling to its owner: the cabin belongs to the servile type.
explanation.definitionFit: Harriet Beecher Stowe's 1852 anti-slavery novel is a famous book.

clue.text: Catch off end of Fisherman's Wharf location

indicators.note: off means taken away, so the front of the city name is removed and its end is left

parts.note: Fisherman's Wharf is a district of San Francisco

explanation.surface: Something caught off the tip of a famous waterfront pier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off end of' leaves the final five letters of SAN FRANCISCO. A cisco is a North American whitefish.
explanation.definitionFit: A cisco is a freshwater fish, something an angler might catch.

clue.text: One of the first names recorded in Somerset House

definitions.text: One of the first names recorded

indicators.note: in tells us the name is concealed within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A forename among the earliest entries held at the old national register office.
explanation.walkthrough: Somerset House in London once held England's register of births. Seth was the third son of Adam, so one of the first names in the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: Seth, son of Adam and Eve, is among the very first people named in Genesis.

clue.text: Evaluate jeep, say, in international campaign

parts.note: a Test is an international cricket or rugby match
a drive is an organised campaign, such as a fundraising drive

explanation.surface: Try out an army vehicle during a worldwide drive.
explanation.definitionFit: To test-drive a vehicle such as a jeep is to try it on the road before buying.

clue.text: Enough to tip the scales, but not right on cue

indicators.note: not right means wrong or out of order, so these letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: Just enough weight to swing a balance, though not exactly at the right moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not right on cue' looks like bad timing; 'not right' is the signal to rearrange ON CUE.
explanation.definitionFit: An ounce is a small unit of weight, a slight amount that could tip a balance.

clue.text: Departs by what method? Ship

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for departs in timetables
how asks in what way something is done

explanation.surface: A traveller leaves and asks how to go: by boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A dhow is an Arab sailing vessel with a lateen sail, a ship.

clue.text: Old man able to hold a lot of drink

definitions.meaning: the patriarch in Genesis said to have lived 969 years

definitions.text: able to hold a lot of drink
definitions.meaning: a very large wine bottle holding eight standard bottles; the clue describes it adjectivally

explanation.surface: An elderly man who can drink a great deal.
explanation.definitionFit: Methuselah is the longest-lived man in the Bible, and also a large champagne bottle.
